fields.meta_title: Subscription Landing Page Builder and Examples | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build a subscription landing page from a prompt. See four examples: a coffee plan picker, a meal kit waitlist, gift plans, and a cleaning plan.
fields.h1: Build a Subscription Landing Page That Sells Recurring Plans
fields.hero_description: Build a subscription landing page where visitors pick a plan and how often it arrives, with each plan saved to a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What Emergent Builds Into a Subscription Page
fields.features_subheading: Emergent builds the plan picker a visitor uses, the form that takes their details, and the table where every new plan waits.
fields.feature_1:
Offers and schedules from one prompt

Describe what you sell and how often it ships. Emergent builds the page around it: the offer, the options a visitor picks from, and a signup form. Prompt again to change it.
fields.feature_2:
The plan price beside the one-time price

Give the app both prices and it shows them side by side for every option, with the saving worked out. Visitors see what a plan costs per delivery before they type an address.
fields.feature_3:
Every subscriber saved as a row you own

The app saves each signup to a database you own, with the product and schedule beside the subscriber's address. Sort the rows by start date to see whose order ships next week.
fields.feature_4:
An alert for each new subscriber

Choose how you hear about new plans, and the app sends an email, Slack message, or in-app alert with the plan attached. A reminder goes out on the day a gift plan starts.
fields.feature_5:
Signups synced to Stripe and HubSpot

The app connects to any tool with an API, such as Stripe or HubSpot, and syncs each new signup in and out. Shipping and email tools get the details the page took, with no retyping.
fields.feature_6:
A page on your domain, code in your repo

Publish on your own domain, such as yourbrand.com; custom domains are included in Emergent and use credits. On paid plans, export the full code of the page to your GitHub repository.

fields.tab_content_1:
Every bag shows its $15.30 plan price beside $18

Larkspur Roasting sells its coffee in 12 oz bags, and its page lets a visitor pick a roast, a grind, and a delivery every 2 or 4 weeks. Each bag shows the $15.30 plan price beside the $18 one-time price, 15% off. In October visitors saved 140 plans, 96 every 2 weeks and 44 every 4 weeks. Ines Varga's plan was one of them.
fields.tab_content_2:
When a zip code is off the route, a waitlist opens

Copperpot Kitchen delivers meal kits to 38 zip codes, and its page asks for a zip code first. Visitors outside them join a waitlist for their zip, and when one zip passes 40 names the app emails the owner, Odile Brandt. In September 212 people joined the waitlist, and one zip reached 41 names with Rafferty Nolan.
fields.tab_content_3:
A $126 gift covers 6 months of tea for Wren

Fernmoor Tea Club's gift page sells 3, 6, or 12 months of its monthly tea box for $66, $126, or $240. The buyer adds the recipient and a start month, and the app emails the recipient a card when the plan starts. Callum Ashdown bought 6 months for Wren Ashdown, starting in December.
fields.tab_content_4:
Bedrooms and visits a month set a $280 plan

Tidewell Home Cleaning prices its plans on the page: a visitor enters bedrooms, picks 1, 2, or 4 visits a month, and sees the price. The app emails each request to the owner, Dario Lindqvist. Marisol Tchakarov chose 2 visits a month for 3 bedrooms, $140 a visit and $280 a month, one of 27 plan requests in October.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Subscription Landing Page
fields.howto_description: Follow these seven steps to price and publish a subscription landing page that saves every new subscriber you sign up.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Name what arrives and how often
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Explain how to skip or cancel
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Ask only what the first delivery needs
fields.howto_step_1_des: Write down what a subscriber gets in each delivery, the sizes you offer, and the schedules you can keep, such as every 2 or 4 weeks. Offer only the schedules your packing and shipping can hold for a full year.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Show both prices on every option, with the saving in dollars or as a percentage. A visitor choosing between one bag and a plan should see the difference at a glance, without doing the math before they decide.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Say in plain words how a subscriber skips a delivery or stops for good, and where they do it. Put that line near the signup button, where a buyer who is weighing a recurring order looks before choosing.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Keep the signup form to what you need to ship or book the first order: name, email, address, and the option chosen. Ask about preferences, such as a favorite roast, once they have subscribed.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Describe the page in one prompt
fields.howto_step_5_des: Paste your offer and your prices into Emergent with any rules you want, such as a zip code check. You get the page and the table that saves every signup, ready for a first test order.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Connect the tools behind each plan
fields.howto_step_6_des: Connect the payment and shipping tools you already use, such as Stripe, and each new signup reaches them without retyping. Choose one tool to hold the subscriber record, where a change of address is made once.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Subscribe to each schedule once with a test order, and check the price and start date in the saved row. When every row is right, publish the page and send the link to your current customers first.

faq_plan.q: What is a subscription landing page?
faq_plan.a: A subscription landing page is a single page that sells a recurring plan, such as a box that ships every month or a cleaning visit booked by the month. It shows what arrives and how often, states the price per delivery, and asks the visitor to choose a plan.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a subscription landing page?
faq_plan.a: Describe what you sell and your delivery schedules in one prompt to Emergent's AI landing page builder. Emergent builds the page with its plan options and a database that saves each subscriber. Change any part by prompting, place a test order, then publish.

faq_plan.q: What should a subscription landing page say above the fold?
faq_plan.a: Say what arrives and what one delivery costs on a plan, and put that price next to the signup button. Add one line on how to skip or cancel there too. Reviews and shipping details can sit lower on the page.

faq_plan.q: Is a subscription landing page different from a page that sells paid access?
faq_plan.a: Yes, in what it leads with. If what you sell arrives on a schedule, such as a refill or a cleaning visit, lead with what ships and how often. If you sell access to a club or a space, a membership landing page fits better, since it leads with tiers and member perks.

faq_plan.q: How do I show the savings on a subscription landing page?
faq_plan.a: Show the plan price and the one-time price side by side on every option, then state the difference once, as a percentage or in dollars per delivery. One figure, such as 15% off each bag, reads faster than a table of rates. Use the same figure everywhere it appears on the page.

faq_plan.q: Should a subscription landing page explain how to cancel?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Tell buyers how to cancel before they choose a plan, and link to the page where subscribers manage it. Use the same words in your confirmation email. In the app Emergent builds, each cancellation can be saved as a row in a database you own.

faq_plan.q: How do I get subscribers to share my subscription landing page?
faq_plan.a: Give each subscriber a personal link and a reward both sides understand, such as a free box for them and 20% off a first box for the friend. Put the offer on the confirmation page and in the first shipping email. A referral landing page can hold the offer and count each signup that arrives from a link.

faq_plan.q: Can a subscription landing page take signups before my first box ships?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Publish the page with a waitlist and a ship date in place of a live plan picker, and save each signup with the plan it wants. That count by plan tells you how much stock to order. Emergent builds the waitlist version from your prompt, and one more prompt changes it to live plans.

faq_plan.q: How do gift plans work on a subscription landing page?
faq_plan.a: A buyer pays for a set number of months on someone else's behalf. Ask the buyer for the length and the recipient's address, plus a short message, and store the recipient's details apart from the buyer's. A note to the recipient before the first box arrives tells them it is coming.

faq_plan.q: How do I make a subscription landing page convert better?
faq_plan.a: Cut the form to what the first order needs, and keep one button on the page. Then test one change at a time, starting with the headline, and keep the version that brings in more plans per visitor. A high converting landing page shows the same habits on offers that do not renew.

plan.angle: The top 10 for subscription landing page is design galleries, template marketplaces, newsletter signup guides and membership site roundups; none builds the page a subscription box, a replenished product or a recurring service actually needs. This page shows four subscription pages built from a prompt and what each does with a visitor: a coffee roaster's plan picker that shows the plan price beside the one-time price, a meal kit's zip code check that sends visitors outside the route to a waitlist for their zip, a tea club's gift plans for 3, 6 or 12 months, and a cleaning company's service plan quote by bedrooms and visits a month. The FAQ covers the definition, the build, what the page must say, savings, price placement, pause and cancel wording, prelaunch signups, gift plans, referrals and conversion. Membership, SaaS and newsletter pages are siblings and stay out; no auto-renewal law claims and no payment processing claims.

Copperpot Kitchen's meal kit page asks for a zip code first; visitors inside its 38 delivery zip codes see the plan picker, the rest join a waitlist for their zip, and when one zip passes 40 names the app emails Odile Brandt: in September 212 people joined the waitlist, 41 of them in one zip, Rafferty Nolan the 41st.

scope.evidence: H1 'Build a Subscription Landing Page That Sells Recurring Plans'; hero 'Build a subscription landing page where visitors pick a plan and how often it arrives, with each plan saved to a database you own.' covers the whole job; how-to description is one sentence on pricing and publishing.

intent.evidence: Top 10 is galleries, templates and examples; page gives four worked examples (coffee plan picker, meal kit waitlist, gift plans, cleaning plan quote), a 7-step how-to and a comparison table. Newsletter, SaaS and membership readings are left to their siblings, which is correct.

specificity.evidence: Buyer vocabulary throughout: 'the $15.30 plan price beside the $18 one-time price', 'Offer only the schedules your packing and shipping can hold for a full year', 'Ask about preferences, such as a favorite roast, once they have subscribed'.

openers.evidence: Feature bodies open on full sentences with verbs: 'Describe what you sell and how often it ships.', 'Give the app both prices...', 'Choose how you hear about new plans...'.

craft.evidence: No blocking craft defect; 13 'A, B, and C' lists (QC Q8) recorded as a note.

voice.evidence: Calm, product-led: 'Sort the rows by start date to see whose order ships next week.' Repetition of 'plan' noted only.

truth.evidence: Claims map to prompt-build, database-owned, alerts, api-connect, custom-domain, code-export ('On paid plans, export the full code of the page to your GitHub repository'). Stripe appears only as an API connection (feature 5 'connects to any tool with an API, such as Stripe or HubSpot', how-to 6 'Connect the payment and shipping tools you already use, such as Stripe'): no payment-processing claim and no auto-renewal-law claim (cancel guidance in step 3 and FAQ 6 is advice). Numbers agree: $18 x 0.85 = $15.30, 96+44 = 140, 2 x $140 = $280, 41 > 40.

distinct.evidence: FAQ 4 separates it from the membership page ('If you sell access to a club or a space, a membership landing page fits better'); no newsletter or SaaS framing; no sibling primary in a heading.

faq.evidence: 10 on-topic questions, answer-first, no brand in any question; hub link in item 2; sibling links to membership, referral and high converting pages; moat lines in FAQ 6 and 8.

images.evidence: Contact sheet matches copy: $18/$15.30 and '140 plans in October, 96 every 2 weeks, 44 every 4'; zip 30318 at 41 names, 'Emailed to Odile', '212 on the waitlist'; $66/$126/$240 with Wren Ashdown, 'Starts in December'; '$280', '$140 a visit', '27 plan requests In October'. One hero each.
